title: Daily Walkaround Checklist
summary: The 27 checks DVSA lists for a lorry's daily walkaround, as a printable checklist, plus how to record defects.

blocks.text: You're responsible for making sure your vehicle is safe to drive. Do a walkaround check before your journey and report any defects in writing to the person in charge of sorting out defects.

blocks.title: In the cab (checks 1–4)
items: Front view: nothing in the swept area of the wipers; windscreen not cracked, scratched, discoloured or over-tinted.
Mirrors in place, not damaged, obscured or insecure. Camera instead of a mirror? Check it works and the view is right.
Wipers work and aren't missing, damaged or worn. Washer works.
Instruments, gauges and warning lights work, including engine, emissions, ABS and EBS warnings.
Steering moves properly, power steering works, no excessive play, no jamming, no lift in the column.

blocks.title: In the cab (checks 5–9)
items: Horn works and is easy to reach from the driver's seat.
Air builds up and the warning system works; no air leaks; footwell clear.
Service brake works tractor and trailer brakes; tractor parking brake works; pedal: no excessive side play, tread intact.
Height marker in the cab shows the correct vehicle height (it can change with the fifth wheel or the load).
Seatbelts: no cuts or fraying, stay secure when plugged in, retract properly.
Cab mountings, tilt devices, panels, doors and steps are secure.

blocks.title: Listen for leaks
blocks.text: After the first brake test, leave the engine running so air pressure can build up. It makes air leaks easier to hear during the rest of the check.

blocks.title: All round (checks 10–18)
items: All lights and indicators work; lenses fitted, clean and the right colour; stop lamps on with the brake; marker lights work.
Fuel cap fitted; no fuel or oil leaks under the vehicle (engine on).
Body, wings, doors, landing legs, sideguards and rear under-run guards secure and undamaged.
Battery secure, in good condition and not leaking.
Enough AdBlue (diesel exhaust fluid); top up if needed.
No excessive exhaust smoke.
High voltage cut-off and fuel isolation switches: know where they are; no leaks or damage.
Spray suppression flaps (if required) fitted, secure, undamaged and not clogged.

blocks.title: Wheels, coupling and load (checks 19–27)
items: Tyres and wheels secure; tread at least 1 mm; correctly inflated; no deep sidewall cuts; no cord visible.
Wheel nuts tight (check wheel nut indicators if fitted); nothing trapped between twin wheels.
Brake lines: couplings clean and in place, no leaks, damage or wear; trailer parking brake works.
Wiring insulated and not likely to get caught; trailer electrical couplings secure; switches work.
Trailer located correctly in the fifth wheel or coupling; secondary locking devices in position.
Load doesn't move and isn't likely to move, with the right securing system.
Number plate, reflectors and markings correct, secure and clean; hazard panels right for dangerous goods.
Other equipment specific to the vehicle, for example loading or specialised equipment.

blocks.title: Record and report
items: Record the registration, date, defects, your assessment (e.g. 'dangerous'), your name and who you told.
No defects? Record 'nil' defects.
Defect found on the road? Stop somewhere safe to assess and report it.

items.text: Dangerous defects MUST be fixed before you continue your journey.

items: DVSA can ask for the record of your walkaround check at a roadside check.
